   Related regularization results for the Ricci flow under critical Ln/2
bounds of Rm have previously been studied in [58, 38] assuming also
pointwise two-sided bounds on |Ric|, and in [53] assuming alternatively
a supercritical kRickp , p > n/2 bound. In this note, we will consider
conditions which are scaling invariant. In particular, we study the
flow under local critical Ln/2 bounds of Rm, but will instead do so in
combination with a Ricci lower bound and control of the local entropy,
a localization of Perelman’s entropy introduced by Wang [54].

measure-space limits of a sequence of smooth manifolds (Mi , gi ) satisfying Theorem 1.1,
or (b) as a Gromov-Hausdorff compactness result for the family of metrics satisfying the
hypotheses of Theorem 1.1. One important thing to point out about Theorem 1.2 is that
the only L∞ assumption on the curvature is that each gi satisfies some uniform lower Ricci
bound, but that bound need not be the same for each i ∈ N.

The second application we present is for manifolds (M, g) that satisfy the hypotheses of
Theorem 1.1 on all scales, thus allowing us to apply the theorem to increasingly extreme
blow-downs to obtain long-time Ricci flow existence with the scale invariant properties (2)
holding for all times. This allows us to conclude topological rigidity and global volume
bounds on the initial manifold.

Remark 1.4. One would expect an ε-regularity theorem holding near a multiplicity Q plane to
imply that any ε-regularity theorem also holds at multiplicity Q′ < Q planes, and so the need in the
above to work with all multiplicities ≤ Q would reduce to working with just multiplicity Q. Indeed,
this is certainly the case when the class V is determined by structural or variational assumptions,
as if V ∈ V was close to a multiplicity Q′ < Q plane P , one could consider V + (Q − Q′ )(P + z) for
a small z ∈ P ⊥ (for which P + z and V are disjoint) and this varifold would also lie in V and now
be close a multiplicity Q plane. However, it is not entirely clear how to deduce this abstractly from
a single regularity result near multiplicity Q planes. To phrase our results appropriately (and since
one expects that in order to verify an ε-regularity theorem near multiplicity Q planes, one needs
to have already verified one near planes of multiplicity < Q) we work with Definition 1.2 as stated.

Remark 1.5. When Q = 2 in Definition 1.2, as soon as one has the conclusion that Ve is represented
by a Lipschitz 2-valued graph, all the subsequent conclusions regarding generalised-C 1,α regularity
and the corresponding estimates follow from [BKMW25]. This is the basis for our application to
the class of Lipschitz 2-valued stationary graphs. It is perhaps reasonable to suspect that the ε-
regularity theorem in [BKMW25] generalises to all Q ∈ {2, 3, 4, . . . }, at which point not only does
the work become applicable to Lipschitz Q-valued stationary graphs, but Definition 1.2 simplifies,
only requiring the conclusion of being represented by a Lipschitz multi-valued graph.

1     Introduction
Let V be a d dimensional integral varifold in an open subset U of Rn that is stationary, i.e.,
δV = 0. By Allard’s theorem (see [All72]) the support of the weight measure ∥V ∥ carries
a d rectifiable structure. That this structure is as smooth as one may presently hope in the absence of
a regularity theory for spt ∥V ∥ itself, was established by Brena, De Lellis and Franceschini [BDLF25].
The purpose of the present paper is to give an alternative proof of their theorem, along a route
that is independent of theirs; we claim no other novelty, and we compare the two arguments in
detail below.

1.1 Theorem (see 10.5 and 10.8). Let U ⊆ Rn be open and let V ∈ IVd (U ) satisfy δV = 0. Then
spt ∥V ∥ is (H d , d) rectifiable of class (k, α) for every k ∈ P and 0 < α < 1; in particular it is
(H d , d) rectifiable of class C ∞ .

    Here rectifiability of class (k, α) (respectively C ∞ ) is understood in the measure-theoretic sense:
the carrier of ∥V ∥ is covered by a countable union of d dimensional submanifolds of class C k,α
(respectively C ∞ ). Equivalently, by the characterisation of Anzellotti–Serapioni and Santilli ([AS94]
and [San19, 1.2, 5.6]), at H d almost every point spt ∥V ∥ admits an approximate Taylor expansion
of order (k, α) (respectively of every finite order). No regularity of spt ∥V ∥ as a set is asserted or
used; the singular examples of stationary varifolds are not excluded, and whether the complement
of Allard’s regular set is H d null remains, after more than fifty years, open.
    The result is the natural endpoint of a sequence of successive improvements. Combining Allard’s
interior regularity with Almgren’s multiple valued functions, as observed by Brakke [Bra78] (the
attribution is made explicitly in [BDLF25, §1]), one obtains rectifiability of class (1, α) for every
α < 1; Menne [Men13] established rectifiability of class C 2 , which is optimal in the wider class
of varifolds of locally bounded first variation. The endpoint was reached by Brena, De Lellis and
Franceschini [BDLF25], whose priority we acknowledge. The present work, begun years before and
carried out in ignorance of theirs, arrives at the same conclusion by different means.
